indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or worn out, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the hyphenated phrase supplies nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sports report on misjudged attempts, with one shot that only just failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like part of the sporting picture, a near-miss attempt, but it signals the rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Solecisms are mistakes in grammar or etiquette, that is, misuses of language or manners.

indicators.note: the answer is on show, visible within the run of letters across the clue's opening words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Harris tweed, the Scottish cloth, always displays its quality of fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris evokes Harris Tweed, a famous cloth from the Scottish island, which makes 'fibre' sit naturally in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff natural fibre from an agave plant, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Freedom may be taken by chancer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: independence or the right to act freely
second meaning: the thing an opportunist takes, from the idiom about overstepping the mark

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint from the idiom 'to take a liberty', meaning to presume too far; a chancer is a British word for an opportunist who tries their luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means independence, and in the idiom it is the presumptuous act an opportunist commits.

clue.text: Ship captured by leaderless mysterious group waiting for delivery of spirits

definitions.text: group waiting for delivery of spirits

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes within the other
without a leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: occult means hidden, secret or mystical
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Sailors held hostage by a strange sect that is waiting for a shipment of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship is Jason's Argo from Greek myth. 'Spirits' looks like drink, but here it means ancestral or supernatural beings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo cult is a Melanesian religious movement whose followers expect goods to be delivered by ancestors or supernatural beings.

clue.text: Dusty season in front of competitors

parts.note: one of the four seasons
the field is all the runners in a race

explanation.surface: A dry time of year comes before the athletes take to the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dusty' looks like an adjective but is the first name of the singer Dusty Springfield, so the definition is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty Springfield was a celebrated British pop and soul singer of the 1960s.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to drain or undermine strength
second meaning: a gullible or foolish person
third meaning: vitality or vigour, as in being full of it

explanation.surface: Something drains a foolish person of their vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition; the possessive 's is only there to make the surface read as a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is a verb meaning drain, a noun for a dupe, and a noun for vigour, like the fluid in a plant.

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the odd-numbered positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: count across both words as one run and keep every other letter starting with the first

explanation.surface: A strangely formal style of Urdu turns out to be counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is an impostor or sham, the same as a fake when used as a noun.

clue.text: End of the trial no fun for criminal

indicators.note: end asks for the final letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the last letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: The close of a court case is miserable for the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' does double duty, linking 'End' to the words and also giving its own last letter. The puzzle has US election references; Elon Musk lurks in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone convicted of a serious crime, so the word is a noun for a criminal.

clue.text: Help for speaker to get gold to stick

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
a cue is the stick used in billiards and snooker

explanation.surface: A speaker urged to go for the gold standard and stay on message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' reads as a verb, keep to, but here it is a noun, the rod used to strike balls on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is a screen showing a script that a presenter or speaker reads while appearing to look at the audience.

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
esse is Latin for to be, used in English for existence or being
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up incognito at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party, a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dressed up is to wear a costume, so the phrase describes someone disguised.

clue.text: Less wasted by Queen wearing damaged robes

damaged things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in tattered ceremonial clothing is less wasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' means drunk, not squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very drunk, so someone less wasted is soberer, the comparative of sober.

clue.text: Range of colours allowed in crown

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Which colours are permitted in a royal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royalty but means the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the board a painter mixes colours on, and by extension the set of colours used.

clue.text: One half of resort hosting leader of right-wing movement

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece goes within the other
only one half of the word is kept and the rest discarded

parts.note: Mar-a-Lago is Donald Trump's Florida resort and club

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A political resort playing host to the head of a right-wing movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is Mar-a-Lago, in keeping with the puzzle's US election references; its second half LAGO wraps the R. 'Movement' looks political but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a tempo marking for very slow playing, and so the name of a slow section of a symphony or sonata.

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant or delightful
knacks are skills or clever tricks

explanation.surface: Charming little sleights of hand performed with small ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Knick-knacks, also spelt nicknacks, are small ornamental objects of little value, the same as trinkets.

parts.note: surface reading: a flood of household animals
setter's reading: a downpour, the heavy rain in a familiar idiom about two common pets

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'raining cats and dogs' describes torrential rain, so a flood of the two common pets is a cloudburst.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used of very heavy rain, an inundation, and literally names two kinds of household animal.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to poke your nose in, to snoop
second meaning: to force open, the American form of prise

explanation.surface: Prod something using a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to meddle nosily and to force something open with a lever.

indicators.note: broken things are smashed into a new arrangement
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: read as 'skin head', the head of skin, its first letter
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A thuggish youth lets the plates fall and smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' splits into 'Skin' and 'head'. 'Broken' does double work: it scrambles the letters and describes the fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsherds are fragments of broken pottery, so the definition is crockery in pieces.

clue.text: Defiant lout at sea not suitable for captain

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A rebellious yob aboard ship is no material for the captaincy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' and 'captain' build a nautical picture; 'at sea' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain leads a team or crew, so someone not suitable for that role is unfit to lead.

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
W is short for with
a ship's helm is its wheel or tiller

explanation.surface: Flatten a set of balls by running a wheel over them.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a cricket term for six deliveries bowled in a row by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an enemy is to defeat them completely, to crush them.

clue.text: Chance the servant will move on

parts.note: a turn is a go or opportunity
taken as written
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: Perhaps the servant will leave his post.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the page is an idiom for leaving the past behind and starting afresh.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who talks on at length without focus
second meaning: a climbing rose with long trailing stems

explanation.surface: A muddled orator got to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the past tense of rise, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler talks in a wandering way, and is also a variety of climbing rose.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: close with a zipper
second meaning: shrink a computer file into an archive

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means both to do up a zipper and to compress computer data into a smaller file.

clue.text: A lot of evil in people

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Zion stands for the Jewish people or homeland
ill as a noun means harm or evil

explanation.surface: There is a great deal of wickedness in humankind.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal word for an enormous, unspecified number, a lot.

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word taken twice

explanation.surface: Awkward men got into twice the difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' tells you to write the word before it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-handed is an informal adjective for awkward or heavy-handed, the same as clumsy.

clue.text: Getting on with a game at midnight

parts.note: taken as written
gin rummy is a card game

indicators.note: mid means take the letter at the very centre of the word

parts.note: read as 'mid night', the middle letter of night

explanation.surface: Playing cards late into the night as one gets on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' splits into 'mid' and 'night'; gin is short for gin rummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing older, which is what aging means.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: renege on a deal or promise

explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a bet is to go back on it, and a native of Cardiff, the capital of Wales, is Welsh.

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it

parts.note: an informal hello
okay means all right

explanation.surface: A forced, polite hello that is only just good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokey is informal for corny or artificially sentimental, meaning contrived.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bounces back, as prices or patients do
second meaning: mass meetings or demonstrations

explanation.surface: Someone recuperates after a round of meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: With the puzzle's election references, the rallies are campaign events.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for regaining strength and a plural noun for large public meetings.

indicators.note: the possessive marks something belonging to and held within the composer's name

parts.note: sits near the end of the composer's name

clue.text: I appear in eccentric bloke's column

the possessive ending joins the letters being rearranged
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall four-sided stone pillar tapering to a point, a type of column.

clue.text: Show indifference when playful roughness avoids nose

taken as written, its letters removed

clue.text: Payment to silence strange hums interrupting sweetheart
